annotationRationale: Tangency classification and counting feasible centers are the central tasks. Both equivalent shared-bank methods are retained: one uses circle-locus intersections, while the other verifies all centers algebraically. Reading circle equations and computing areas are shared prerequisites.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independent tangency classification gives only radii 3 and 5, with center distances 5 and 3 from the origin respectively. Each radius has four feasible centers, so the area sum is \(4\pi(9+25)=136\pi\), choice E. No stem, choice, or figure contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both supplied shared methods from 2022_AMC_10B_Q22 are retained and independently verified: count-center-locus-intersections and solve-center-distance-equations. The former gives geometric feasibility, while the latter verifies all real centers algebraically. LIVE and AoPS supply equivalent geometric and coordinate routes, so no further method is beneficial.
review.annotationCheck: Circle-position classification is appropriately assessed. Reading circle equations and computing areas are supports. The coordinate method's quadratic-system elimination is correctly method-local; the locus method needs no separate triangle-inequality node because cnm_h181 explicitly includes the two-intersection criterion used.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The exclusions force d+r=8. Tangency to the inner circle then gives exactly (r,d)=(3,5) or (5,3). For q=r±√3, all four cases satisfy the strict two-intersection inequalities, producing two centers each. Distinct q values prevent overlap within a radius case, and differing radii distinguish the other cases. The total is 136π.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses amc/2022_AMC_10B_Q22#count-center-locus-intersections. The shared reference and both inherited LIVE and AoPS reference IDs are retained exactly. The table adapts credited project prose and does not claim official MAA provenance.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Containment exclusions, both inner-circle tangency types, and both third-circle tangency types are explained. The table's bounds follow from 1<√3<2, and its factors of two and final totals are justified.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h181 covers both tangency classification and center-locus intersection counts. cnm_h176 supplies the given centers and radii, and cnm_p192 supplies the final areas.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The circle-position link is appropriately partial because the canonical definition corrects coincidence cases; all cases here are nondegenerate. The standard-circle-equation and area links are exact for their uses.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The circle-equation links provide limited overlap with reading and using a circle locus, without deriving equations or completing squares. 7.G.B.4 supports the area calculation only; no circumference or formula derivation is shown. No supplied US link covers the central two-circle position skill.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three direct IDs fit precisely. The intersection inequalities are explicitly within cnm_h181, so no additional intermediate-result node is required.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The two possible (r,d) pairs are complete. Subtracting squared distance equations gives u=(19±3√3)/5 for radius 3 and u=3/5±√3 for radius 5. The stated bounds ensure positive v² in all four cases, hence two real centers each. Positive required distances recover unsquared tangency, yielding eight distinct circles and area sum 136π.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly reuses amc/2022_AMC_10B_Q22#solve-center-distance-equations. Its shared reference and both original LIVE and AoPS provenance IDs remain in sourceRefIds. The project reuse and third-party-informed basis are accurately described.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The subtraction explains the coordinate strategy. Both radius cases explicitly verify real feasibility, distinctness, and recovery of the original distances, so the argument does not rely on a sketch or an unsupported symmetry count.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The circle-position and standard-equation nodes support the setup. math:quadratic-system-elimination precisely covers shared-square elimination, real recovery, and original-domain checking. cnm_p192 covers the area total.
